name: REST APIs & HTTP
description: Understanding HTTP and designing, calling and debugging RESTful web APIs.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is normally used to retrieve a resource without modifying it?
questions.explanation: GET is a safe method intended only for retrieval.

questions.question: What does HTTP status code 404 mean?
questions.explanation: 404 Not Found means the server cannot find the requested resource.

questions.question: Which set of methods is idempotent according to HTTP semantics?
questions.explanation: Repeating GET, PUT or DELETE leaves the server in the same state as doing it once; POST is not idempotent and PATCH is not guaranteed to be.

questions.question: What is the difference between 401 and 403 responses?
options: 401 means the server is down; 403 means the URL is wrong
401 means authentication is missing or invalid; 403 means the client is identified but not allowed
403 means rate limited; 401 means bad JSON
questions.explanation: 401 Unauthorized asks for valid credentials; 403 Forbidden refuses access even though the identity may be known.

questions.question: A page on https://a.com calls fetch('https://api.b.com/data') and the browser blocks reading the response unless b.com sends an Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. Which mechanism is this?
options: The same-origin policy, relaxed via CORS
questions.explanation: Browsers enforce the same-origin policy; Cross-Origin Resource Sharing headers let a server opt in to cross-origin reads.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate response to a successful POST that creates a new resource?
options: 201 Created with a Location header pointing to the new resource
questions.explanation: 201 Created signals creation, and the Location header tells the client where the new resource lives.

practical.title: Create a user with curl
practical.instructions: Write a curl command that sends a POST request to https://api.example.com/users with the JSON body {"name": "Asha"} and the header Content-Type: application/json. Then state in one sentence which status code you expect on successful creation.
practical.expected_output: curl -X POST https://api.example.com/users -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name": "Asha"}' and a note that 201 Created is expected.

rubric.description: Uses curl to send a POST
rubric.hint: Use curl -X POST (or -d, which implies POST).

rubric.description: Sends the name in the body

rubric.hint: Successful resource creation should return 201 Created.

tasks.title: Learn how HTTP works
tasks.description: Read the MDN HTTP overview and the pages on methods, headers and status codes. Use your browser's developer tools Network tab to inspect requests made by a real website.
tasks.completion_criteria: You can explain request/response structure and the meaning of 2xx, 3xx, 4xx and 5xx codes.

tasks.title: Call public APIs with curl
tasks.description: Use curl to make GET and POST requests against a public test API, adding headers and query parameters. Inspect response headers with -i and verbose output with -v.
tasks.completion_criteria: A notes file with 5 working curl commands and what each response showed.

tasks.title: Design a REST API
tasks.description: Design resource URLs, methods, status codes and JSON shapes for a simple bookstore API including pagination and error responses. Write it up as an OpenAPI or markdown spec.
tasks.completion_criteria: A spec covering at least 6 endpoints with correct methods and status codes.

tasks.title: Build and document a REST API
tasks.description: Implement the bookstore API with a framework of your choice, backed by a database, with input validation, authentication and proper error codes. Test it with automated tests and curl.
tasks.completion_criteria: Running API with CRUD endpoints, authentication, validation errors returning 4xx, and passing tests.
